NPTEL Online Certification Course
             Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee
Course Name: Introduction to Application of Artificial Intelligence to Robotics
                             Instructor: Prof. Pushparaj Mani Pathak

                 WEEK 1: ASSIGNMENT 1


   Q.1   Consider where the task of robot is instructed to protect itself even if it is about to
         harm a human. Which Asimov law(s) is/are violated?

         (A) Law 1

          (B) Law 2

          (C) Law 3

         (D) All of the above

          Explanation: (A)

          Refer Slide: 26. This directly violates the First Law, because harming a human is
          never allowed. The Third Law only permits self-protection when it does not conflict
          with the First Law.


   Q.2   Which of the following is NOT a benefit of offline programming?

         (A) Reduced robot downtime during programming

          (B) Integration with CAD databases

          (C) Continuous production during program development

         (D) Elimination of robot calibration requirements

          Explanation: (D)

          Refer Slide: 44-47

        Even if a program is created offline, the real robot must be calibrated so that its
          coordinate system matches the virtual model. Without proper calibration, the robot
        may miss target positions, collide with objects, or produce inaccurate results.


   Q.3   Which statement correctly differentiates Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning
          (DL), and Reinforcement Learning (RL)?

         (A) ML learns from rewards, DL uses decision trees, RL requires labeled data.

          (B) ML learns from data, DL uses deep neural networks, RL learns through rewards
         and penalties.

          (C) ML only works on images, DL only works on text, RL only works on robots.

         (D) All three methods require manually programmed rules.

Q.4  A robot vacuum decides where to move next based only on its current location and
       not on previously visited rooms. This illustrates:

      (A) Reward Function

      (B) Markov Property

      (C) Discount Factor

      (D) Transition Model

       Explanation: (B)

      Refer Slide: 28 of Lecture: 2


Q.5    In the state equation
                                         𝑥̇(𝑡) = 𝐴𝑥(𝑡) + 𝐵𝑢(𝑡)

       the term 𝑢(𝑡)represents:

      (A) Output

      (B) Input (control signal)

      (C) State variable

      (D) System matrix

       Explanation: (B)

      Refer Slide: 18 of Lecture: 3


Q.6   Given
                                𝑓(𝑥, 𝑦) = 3𝑥2 + 2𝑥𝑦+ 𝑦2
      Find the gradient at (1, 2).

      (A) [8, 4]

      (B) [10, 6]

      (C) [6, 10]

      (D) [12, 8]

Explanation: (B)

      Refer Slide: 9 of Lecture: 3

                         ∂𝑓         ∂𝑓
                   ∂𝑥= 6𝑥+ 2𝑦, ∂𝑦= 2𝑥+ 2𝑦
      At (1, 2):

                           ∂𝑓
                     ∂𝑥= 6(1) + 2(2) = 10
                           ∂𝑓
                     ∂𝑦= 2(1) + 2(2) = 6
       Therefore,

                                  ∇𝑓(1,2) = [10 ] .
                                       6



Q.7    Probabilistic models are particularly useful in robotics because they:

      (A) Eliminate uncertainty.

      (B) Ignore sensor measurements.

      (C) Model sensor noise and real-world uncertainty.

      (D) Always produce the shortest path.

       Explanation: (C)

      Refer Slide: 12 of Lecture: 4


Q.8  A robotics engineer models an autonomous vehicle as a single point moving on a 2D
     map to quickly test path-planning algorithms. This model primarily has:

      (A) High fidelity and high resolution

      (B) High fidelity and low resolution

      (C) Low fidelity and low resolution

      (D) Low fidelity and high resolution

       Explanation: (C)

      Refer Slide: 18 of Lecture: 4

      The model ignores many real-world details and represents the vehicle with minimal
        detail.

slides.title: Q.9  A robotics team develops a navigation module independently of the speech
slides.text:
Q.9  A robotics team develops a navigation module independently of the speech
       recognition module. Later, both modules are integrated without modifying their
        internal code. Which ROS design principle does this illustrate?

      (A) Inheritance

      (B) Modularity

      (C) Encapsulation

      (D) Deterministic execution

       Explanation: (B)

      Refer Slide: 9 of Lecture: 5


Q.10  Which statement is TRUE?

      (A) TF stores and updates the spatial relationships between coordinate frames.

      (B) TF defines the robot's links and joints.

      (C) URDF continuously updates the robot's pose while it moves.

      (D) URDF publishes camera images.

       Explanation: (A)

      Refer Slide: 33 of Lecture: 5
